subject.title: bug(slack): slash commands (/compact /new /stop) are silently inert in Slack DMs — no recovery path for wedged sessions

question: Should Slack DM text recovery commands be authorized for admitted DM users, restricted to the owner allowlist with visible denial, or moved to a safer Slack-specific recovery path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair changes who can trigger owner-like session controls from open Slack DMs, which is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Owner-gated with visible denial
options.body: Keep command execution behind owner/access-group authorization, but make Slack DM `/compact`, `/new`, and `/stop` return an actionable denial or recovery instruction when unauthorized.

options.title: Authorize admitted DM senders
options.body: Treat users admitted by Slack open-DM policy as authorized for recovery commands, improving self-service recovery but expanding who can reset, compact, or stop sessions.

options.title: Add a safe Slack recovery path
options.body: Keep owner commands blocked and add a narrower Slack DM recovery action that cannot trigger broader owner-only controls.

recommendation.title: Owner-gated with visible denial
recommendation.body: Keep command execution behind owner/access-group authorization, but make Slack DM `/compact`, `/new`, and `/stop` return an actionable denial or recovery instruction when unauthorized.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits closest to recent Slack ingress and authorization history, and the Slack owner boundary is the main unresolved decision.
